text:
marta: Postmortem-style recap from yesterday's late-night perf run. Main takeaway: synchronous compaction during admission causes observable p99 jumps. Need a safer scheduling contract.
vince: Do we have numbers? IIRC the run with immediate compaction showed +220ms p99 vs shaping-first.
doug: Yep. Shaping (coalesce-on-write) cut the median compaction work, and the batcher could handle most churn without an explicit reclaim.
marta: So two knobs: (1) lightweight telemetry (compactness + head_gap) and (2) two-stage control (shaping hint -> reclaim/token). Propose moving to that model.
nina: Love the two-stage idea. Important: reclaim must be lease-protected and idempotent. Also need a small TTL on tokens.
vince: Suggestion: keep reclaim disabled by default and expose shaping + compactness first. That should get 70% of wins with zero RPC risk.
doug: Agreed. For the rare cases where reclaim is necessary we need to define exact semantics: reclaimed slots are not free until scheduler redeems a token. Otherwise races happen.
marta: Wire sketch (plain text):
GET /batcher/metrics -> {lane, occupancy_pct, head_gap_ms, compactness_level}
POST /batcher/shaping -> {lane, lease_id} => {shaped:true, est_freed:int, hold_ms:int}
POST /batcher/reclaim -> {lane, lease_id, target:int, idempotency_key} => {job_id}
POST /batcher/reclaim/ack -> {job_id} => {freed:int, credits_token:str, reserve_ms:int}
POST /scheduler/credits/redeem -> {credits_token, amount} => {redeemed:true}

(Note: this is a sketch; full proto in RFC)
vince: A couple of safety details: (a) idempotency_key returns same job_id on retries, (b) reclaim/ack must persist tokens to stable storage until expiry, (c) batcher should refuse reclaim if ownership_version mismatch.
nina: Observability: emit reclaim.{started,progress,partial,finished}, token.{issued,redeemed,expired}. Also track latency between ack and redeem (credits.latency).
doug: Add a shaping metric: shaped_ratio over last N windows so scheduler can prefer lanes where shaping is effective.
marta: Cancellation: POST /batcher/reclaim/cancel?job=...&lease_id=... -> {cancelled:true, freed_partial:int}. This is needed when owner changes mid-job.
vince: Perf tests: high-churn microrequests + lane migration mid-reclaim. Measure p50/p95/p99 and credits redemption delay. We'll simulate partial failures (batcher crash mid-compact).
nina: Failure mode: acked token lost due to storage failure. Mitigation: batcher must store token durability-first, but if it fails, scheduler TTL will expire and we'll fall back to conservative admission. Document in RFC.
doug: On the scheduler side, prefer consuming reserved credits before admitting new tokens. If multiple schedulers talk to same lane, ownership invariant prevents double-issue. But add guard rails.
marta: Rollout plan: (1) expose /metrics and shaping endpoint behind FF on canary (5%), (2) run perf with shaping enabled, (3) enable reclaim in lab only and run extended tests, (4) if stable, enable reclaim slowly with telemetry.
qa-bot: canary-schedule: batcher-shape-ff -> canary 5% us-east at 03:00 UTC. Healthchecks 15m.
vince: Action items: marta -> draft RFC with full proto + failure scenarios; doug -> add shaping export and token persistence in batcher; nina -> dashboard for token lifecycle and credits.latency; I'll own perf harness.
doug: One more runtime tweak: make shaping responses include a "confidence" value [0-1] so scheduler can weight shaped frees in its heuristic.
nina: Also include a short hold window (hold_ms) where batcher marks freed slots as "reserved" to avoid immediate reuse by other work. Scheduler will claim via redeem.
marta: Ok, I'll assemble these pieces into the RFC and ping for review. Keep reclaim gated until we have token durability and TTL semantics nailed down.
vince: +1. Thanks all.
qa-bot: test-plan-created: batcher-shaping-e2e with bursty traces and lane-migration scenarios.
